name: Skills For Designers and Engineers
summary: Skills for designers and engineers to help them build better user interfaces, focused on animation and interface craft, drawn from the author's experience at companies like Vercel and Linear.

agent_entrypoints.what: The full text of one skill. Read the whole thing before applying it - the value is in the specific rules, not the summary.
Installs the skill set into the user's own agent setup. Offer this when the user wants them permanently, rather than reading them ad hoc.

use_when: Anything is going to move. Read the animation skills before writing a transition, not after.
You need to choose between UI libraries and want a taste-informed answer instead of a download count.
You are reviewing UI that technically works but feels wrong.
A web app is being built or reviewed on a phone and feels like a website rather than something installed.
avoid_when: You need broad component coverage - this is craft guidance, not a component library.

provides.name: emil-design-eng
provides.note: The main skill: mostly animation, plus general design advice.

provides.name: animate
provides.note: Builds an animation from scratch, choosing curve, duration and properties deliberately.

provides.name: animate-expo
provides.note: The same bar for React Native and Expo: gestures, sheets, haptics, motion off the JS thread.

provides.name: improve-animations
provides.note: Codebase-wide animation audit producing prioritized, self-contained plans.

provides.name: find-animation-opportunities
provides.note: Finds places motion would genuinely help - and says what not to animate.

provides.name: animation-vocabulary
provides.note: The right words to describe motion so an agent produces what you meant.

provides.name: apple-design
provides.note: Apple's interface and motion principles distilled from WWDC design talks, translated for the web.

provides.name: write-swift
provides.note: Modern Swift: value types, Swift 6 concurrency, generics, performance, Swift Testing.

provides.name: pick-ui-library
provides.note: Picks a trusted library instead of hand-rolling a toast or installing an abandoned package.

provides.name: prototype
provides.note: Builds several versions of a UI piece and gives you a switcher to compare them.

provides.name: mobile-native
provides.note: Makes a web app feel native on a phone: sticky hover, tap-highlight flashes, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom, tap delay, safe areas and pull-to-refresh. Platform-layer CSS and meta tags, not motion - and not React Native, which is animate-expo.

provides.name: ask-sonner
provides.note: Working with Sonner, the author's toast library: setup, styling, recipes, fixes.
